blocks.content: The National Food Security Act, 2013 marks a paradigm shift in the approach to food security from welfare to a rights-based approach.

items: Note the coverage ratio: 75% rural and 50% urban, covering approximately two-thirds (67%) of the national population.
Remember the issue prices under TPDS: Rice at ₹3/kg, Wheat at ₹2/kg, Coarse grains at ₹1/kg.
Women Empowerment Clause: The eldest woman of 18 years or above is designated as the Head of Household for ration cards.
Maternity benefit provision: Minimum ₹6,000 financial support for pregnant women and lactating mothers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NFSA 2013 legally entitles up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population to receive subsidized foodgrains under TPDS.
Foodgrains are provided at subsidized prices of ₹3/kg for rice, ₹2/kg for wheat, and ₹1/kg for coarse grains.
Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households continue to receive 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month.
Pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to free meals and a maternity benefit of not less than ₹6,000.
The eldest woman aged 18 years or above in a household is designated as the head of the household for issuing ration cards.
